artists.biography:
The Mission, known as The Mission UK in the United States, are an English gothic rock band formed in Leeds in 1986 by vocalist and guitarist Wayne Hussey and bassist Craig Adams, both former members of the Sisters of Mercy. The original lineup was completed by drummer Mick Brown of Red Lorry Yellow Lorry and guitarist Simon Hinkler. Emerging from the mid-1980s post-punk scene, the group developed a dramatic sound built on expansive guitar work, melodic bass lines, atmospheric keyboards, and Hussey’s distinctive, resonant vocals.

The band established its reputation with God’s Own Medicine (1986), followed by the influential albums Children (1988) and Carved in Sand (1990). Later releases including Masque, Neverland, Blue, Aura, God Is a Bullet, The Brightest Light, and Another Fall from Grace reflected their continuing evolution across gothic rock, darkwave, and darker alternative styles. Through lineup changes, breakups, reunions, and sustained touring, The Mission became one of the defining bands of British gothic rock, helping shape the genre’s grand, romantic, and emotionally charged sound.

lastfm.wiki_content: Children is the second regular studio album by the British rock-band The Mission. It was recorded September-December 1987 in The Manor Studios, Oxfordshire, England and released in February 1988 by Mercury Records. Two singles were released from the album, "Tower of Strength" and "Beyond the Pale". A third single, 'Kingdom Come' was scheduled but appeared as a promo-only. The album was re-issued in 2007 with four bonus tracks. Personnel The Mission Craig Adams – bass guitar Mick Brown – drums Simon Hinkler – guitar Wayne Hussey – vocals & guitar Additional musicians John Paul Jones – keyboards & programming Julianne Regan – additional voice on "Beyond The Pale" and "Black Mountain Mist" Jez Webb – harmonica on "Shamera Kye" Michael Ade – violin on "Shamera Kye" Skaila Kenga – Celtic harp on "Black Mountain Mist" Woodstock Infant School – additional voices on "Heat" and "Hymn (for America)" Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Children is The Mission’s second studio album, originally released in 1988 and later issued by Demon Records as a limited Sunshine Yellow vinyl reissue. It finds the British band expanding their gothic-rock foundations into a more polished, melodic form of rock and pop, built around layered guitars, dramatic arrangements, and Wayne Hussey’s resonant vocals. The album’s expansive sound balances dark romanticism with strong hooks and theatrical momentum, reflecting The Mission’s growing confidence after God’s Own Medicine.

As a key release in the band’s early catalogue, Children helped establish their distinctive blend of atmospheric guitar rock and anthemic songwriting. Its broad, carefully produced textures anticipate the even more ambitious Carved in Sand, while retaining the mystique and grandeur associated with late-1980s gothic rock. The Demon Records reissue presents the original album in a collectible new format, bringing its ornate, emotionally charged sound back to vinyl.
